subject: Noise term added when using A-matrix (control.predictor=list(A=Amatrix)

messages.author: e7cc390b005447b3
messages.subject: Noise term added when using A-matrix (control.predictor=list(A=Amatrix)
parts:
Hi,

If I understand it correctly, INLA adds a noise term to the Ax -term if one uses control.predictor=list(A=Amatrix)

I think INLA estimates (Ax,x) or something similar, which means the field is doubled. 

Is it possible to bypass this "extra extension"? I only want Ax and not x, or x but not calculate Ax, as Ax can be found by calculations "after" performing the main estimation. 

Also, constraints can be enforced using the usual rules?
I.e if we want to find(Ax)|Bx=0, we can use the kriging formula. It (roughly) becomes (see Rue's "green"-colored book):

x^*=Ax - AQ^(-1)AB (BAQ^(-1)AB^T)^(-1)(BAx)
(As Ax has variance-covariance matrix AQ^(-1)A)
I have not carried out the calculations carefully, so the above expression may not be 100 % correct.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Noise term added when using A-matrix (control.predictor=list(A=Amatrix)
parts:
you can bypass this by creating a singular model component. The joint
posterior will then be proper or improper depending on the likelihood
components in the model, which is hard to verify upfront. Numerical
errors will also be an issue as singularities (like two elements are
perfectly correlated) can (or rather will) be wrongly interpreted
(numerically) as a non-pos-def matrix instead of a pos-semi-def matrix.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Noise term added when using A-matrix (control.predictor=list(A=Amatrix)
parts:
Hi,

A few comments (Haavard answered a different aspect of some of this) :

The control.predictor A matrix doesn’t mean “Ax is estimated”, but rather it defines the link between the latent variables and the observed values, and it’s the latent variables that are estimated.
Further, the way this works internally has changed drastically with the new default inla.mode=“compact”.

In the old inla.mode=“classic” (that used to be the default until ca January 2023), inla did do the explicit double extension. The regular model matrix, let’s call it B (not related to your constraint B ), was linked directly to the latent variables as
eta=B x
and the predictor linked to the observations was
eta*=A eta
and the observations were linked to eta*. Both of those steps had a near-singular connection in the joint precision matrix, and the internal model was for the extended space (observation link, eta*, eta, x).

In the new default “compact” mode that is no longer the case, and the internal model representation work directly with the latent variables x, and the observations are linked directly to ABx.

The resulting internal precision matrix may still have a small added epsilon on the diagonal to avoid the other types of singularities (due to the model components themselves; this is what Haavard mentioned), but the stepwise construction singularities due to the deterministic eta*=A eta connection are no longer there.

Now, your question is also about whether one could work directly with Ax instead (or really ABx ! ), but he main problem with that is that one would typically lose sparsity.
When x has Markov structure, A x usually doesn’t. So it’s usually more efficient to do the computations for x, and then only compute the distributional properties of A x afterwards, which I think is what’s happening internally in the new inla.mode.

Finn
